title: Adobe Patches 140 Vulnerabilities Across 10 Products
content_md: Adobe has published 10 new security advisories to inform customers about roughly 140 vulnerabilities found and patched in its products. Adobe ColdFusion updates address 32 vulnerabilities, including critical bugs that can be exploited for code execution and privilege escalation. A significant number of flaws have been patched by Adobe in the Content Credentials SDK. The product received fixes for 30 vulnerabilities, many described as high-severity issues that can lead to a security feature bypass. Some security holes can be exploited to cause a DoS condition. Adobe patched 18 vulnerabilities in Photoshop, nearly all allowing arbitrary code execution. In Substance 3D Stager, Adobe fixed 16 vulnerabilities, including many high-severity arbitrary code execution flaws. Eleven vulnerabilities have been resolved in Adobe Commerce, including several critical issues that can be exploited without authentication to execute code or escalate privileges. Several vulnerabilities that allow arbitrary code execution have been fixed in each of the following products: FrameMaker, Dimension, Substance 3D Sampler, Substance 3D Designer, and Bridge. Adobe says it’s not aware of any in-the-wild exploitation. Most advisories have a priority rating of 3, which indicates Adobe does not expect to see these vulnerabilities exploited in attacks. Commerce is the only product with a priority rating of 2 (threat actors have historically targeted Commerce ). Adobe
